prompted_for: Documentation package (became DocList: document code tiles)
composition: desktop artboard in a thin frame left, phone artboard right
brand and hamburger top, two-line caps headline
ten tiles: 3+3 row then 2+2 wide rows
layout_devices: number + slash + document code as tile heading ('01 / FS')
short steel-blue tab bar on each tile's top edge
revision code tag top-right of each tile
motion_implied: plus rotates to minus when a tile opens
t2i_keywords: short steel-blue tab bar on each tile
t2i_prompt: Dark navy web section listing <CONTENT> as a document register: a grid of square outline tiles inside a thin drawing-sheet frame, each headed by a large monospace number, a slash and a short code, a two-line mono caps description, a small revision tag top-right, a plus icon bottom-right and a short steel-blue tab bar on its top edge. Corner registration ticks. Beside it, a phone artboard with the same items as a single-column ruled list. Flat vector, off-white type, one cool accent, square corners, sober and auditable.
signature_idea: The deliverables read like a real document register with codes and revisions, so the package looks audit-ready.
strengths: speaks directly to validation and QA readers
codes and revision tags signal document control
phone list is simple and legible
weaknesses: some listed documents (weld logs, surface finish) fit stainless, not PP
plus icons imply drill-down content that may not exist
brand_fit_why: Navy, square cells, one steel-blue tab accent and mono figures fit well; headlines should be Geist light, not mono caps.
